basis: Childhood-onset generalized epilepsy is a disorder of brain function.
Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma is a skeletal-muscle-lineage malignancy; other DICER1-associated tumours are separate diseases or risks.
Early mycobacterial infection with characteristic skin lesions; substantial peripheral nerve damage is not established as common in this early form.
Cerebellar malformation and developmental impairment define disease; ptosis affects 7/10. Retinal dystrophy alone is below threshold at 2/9.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising in the synovial lining of a joint.
Abnormal recession of the eyeball within the orbit.
Inherited angle-closure glaucoma affects ocular drainage and the optic nerve.
Umbrella for inherited nervous system disorders; muscle and other organ involvement are not shared across most subtypes.
Hereditary hair disorder with sparse scalp hair in 4/4 patients.
Tuberculous infection directly affects bones and joints; pulmonary disease is not required.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy classified as an ST3GAL3 congenital disorder of glycosylation; hypotonia does not establish muscle disease.
Defining abnormalities are absent nails and congenital absence or splitting of digits.
Respiratory-chain deficiency with leukodystrophy, regression and spasticity (4/5); hypotonia alone does not establish direct muscle damage.
Macular retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy with abnormal lipofuscin accumulation.
Acute malignant proliferation of undifferentiated haematopoietic blasts in blood and marrow.
Heterotaxy with cardiac septation defects; sinusitis 2/2, chronic otitis 2/3, intestinal malrotation/atresia each 1/3. Situs inversion alone is not damage.
Umbrella for impaired vision; neurologic causes occur in some subtypes but are not shared across the group.
Inherited focal epilepsy arising in the temporal lobe.
Visually triggered occipital seizures are cerebral; photosensitivity does not establish eye damage.
Defining skin elastin abnormalities and retinal degeneration; cutis laxa and rod-cone dystrophy are obligate.
Intellectual disability and skeletal malformations define syndrome; bilateral ptosis occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac and urinary anomalies are occasional.
PINK1-associated Parkinson disease causes neurodegeneration; rigidity and dystonia are neurologic, and urgency does not establish urinary tract damage.
AARS-related encephalopathy with an inborn amino acid-processing disorder ancestor; hip dislocation 2/3 and rocker-bottom feet 3/3 support skeletal involvement.
Lens displacement defines disease; supplied HPO reports joint stiffness 80-99% and cognitive impairment 30-79%, although atypical for an isolated eye disorder.
Immune-mediated lichen planus with blistering skin lesions; common damaging involvement of additional organs is not established.
